structures.name: kidney
structures.definition: Bean-shaped organ, one on each side of the spine at the back of the abdomen, from about T12 to L3.
structures.function: Filters the blood to make urine, balancing water, salts and acid, and makes renin and erythropoietin.
structures.why: Constant filtering keeps the blood’s chemistry stable whatever we eat and drink.

notes.nursing: Urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/hour is an early warning of acute kidney injury.
notes.medicine: The right kidney sits lower than the left because the liver is above it.

structures.name: adrenal gland
structures.definition: Small triangular gland sitting on top of each kidney.
structures.why: Its outer layer controls salt and stress hormones; its core releases the “fight or flight” hormone.

notes.nursing: Never stop long-term steroids suddenly: the suppressed glands can’t respond to stress (adrenal crisis).

structures.name: renal artery
structures.definition: Artery leaving each side of the aorta at about L1 to enter the kidney.
structures.function: Carries about a fifth of the heart’s output to the kidney.
structures.why: Filtering needs a huge blood flow relative to the organ’s size.

notes.medicine: Narrowing causes hypertension that resists treatment; ACE inhibitors can then worsen kidney function.

structures.name: renal vein
structures.definition: Vein draining each kidney into the inferior vena cava.
structures.function: Returns filtered blood from the kidney to the heart.
structures.why: It carries the cleaned blood back into the circulation.

notes.medicine: The left one is longer and passes in front of the aorta; it also receives the left gonadal vein.

structures.name: ureter
structures.definition: Narrow muscular tube about 25 cm long carrying urine from each kidney down to the bladder.
structures.function: Moves urine to the bladder by waves of contraction.
structures.why: Entering the bladder at an angle stops urine flowing back up when the bladder squeezes.

notes.medicine: Stones lodge at its narrowest points: where it leaves the kidney, crosses the pelvic brim and enters the bladder.
notes.nursing: Loin-to-groin colicky pain with blood in the urine suggests a stone; give analgesia and strain the urine.

structures.name: urinary bladder
structures.definition: Hollow muscular bag in the pelvis behind the pubic bone.
structures.function: Stores urine and empties it under voluntary control.
structures.why: Storage lets us pass urine at convenient times instead of continuously.

notes.nursing: Use a bladder scan before catheterising for retention; record residual volume.
notes.physio: Pelvic floor training improves stress incontinence.

structures.name: urethra
structures.definition: Tube carrying urine from the bladder to the outside; in males it also carries semen.
structures.why: Its sphincters keep it closed until we choose to empty the bladder.

notes.nursing: Use strict aseptic technique for catheterisation; the male urethra is about 20 cm long, the female about 4 cm.
